# ManateeCreekSystems: what it can do, and how it got here

The one-page public website for Manatee Creek Systems LLC (manateecreeksystems.com), served as static files from a single index.html.

## How we got here

Every change entry, newest first: what it was for, and what it made possible.

### 20261031-sophos-skill-1-4-2

Task `skill-sync-sophos-1-4-2-argus-mcs-20261031`.

**Why.** ManateeCreekSystems held the sophos skill at v1.4.1, missing the 23-line re-bootstrap block that tells an agent to redo the whole bootstrap when it expires, so an agent here would not be told to.

**Enables.** An agent working in this repo is told the same expiry rule as every other household repo, and skill-sync reports this repo in sync with the source instead of one version behind.

**Untested:** A copy of one skill file from its source; the bytes were compared by sha256 against Project-Sophos main and the copy loses nothing, since its only exclusive line was the version line.

### 20261028-change-record-in-manateecreeksystems

Task `change-record-deploy-repos-20261028`.

**Why.** ManateeCreekSystems had no record of why its code changes: a commit message keeps what changed, not why it mattered, and the reason lived only in the memory of whoever made it. Ken asked on 2026-10-27 for the household change record in every repository, tuned to each.

**Enables.** Every commit that changes the one-page site now carries why it mattered and what it enables, judged when it is made; the page mixes copy, style and behaviour, so every change to it is judged.

**Untested:** This commit installs the gate here; the engine and this repository's tuning are tested in Project-Sophos, in admin/tests/change-record.test.mjs and admin/tests/change-record-deploy.test.mjs.

*Soli Deo Gloria.*
